newsitem.title: CHINA: New China firms exaggerate profit outlook - brokers.
newsitem.headline: New China firms exaggerate profit outlook - brokers.

text.p: Some firms newly listed in Shanghai have unsettled the stock market by issuing overly optimistic targets for annual profits and posting poor interim results, brokers said on Monday.
They called on the securities authorities to ask the companies involved to explain the big discrepancy between their profit goals and their actual performance.
Brokers said one prominent example was Nanjing Chemical Fibre Co, which makes fibres for the textile industry.
The firm predicted a net profit for the whole of 1996 of 32.13 million yuan ($3.87 million), but had first-half profits of only 710,000 yuan, or only 2.2 percent of its annual target.
Another was Yaohua Glass Co, which promised in a prospectus in July that it could achieve net profit of 79.64 million yuan in 1996.
But, in its interim earnings report in August, it reported first-half profits of 8.83 million yuan, or 11.14 percent of the target.
Officials from the firms could not immediately be contacted for comment.
"Some firms exaggerated their annual targets," said a broker with a major Chinese brokerage. "They should have known what they could achieve this year when forecasting 1996 results."

"The glass and chemical fibre industries have been in a depression since the second half of 1994," said a second broker. "How could the firms (in these industries) fail to predict their 1996 results more accurately?"
Brokers said about one fifth of the 60 firms which have listed in Shanghai so far this year achieved less than 40 percent of their annual net targets in the first half.
They include Shashi Power 28 (Group) Co, which achieved 15.36 percent and Songliao Automobile Co, an automaker owned by the Chinese army, with 14.85 percent.

"Whenever a new firm posts worse-than-expected results after predicting high annual targets, its share price falls sharply, causing instability on the market," said a third broker. "This damages the reputation of the company."
On the day it published its interim results, Nanjing Chemical Fibre's share price fell four percent. Qinhuangdao plunged 26.2 percent.
Brokers said company prospectuses and listing statements were major ways for investors to judge a firm's performance, and predicting unrealistic results was unfair for investors.
"They (unrealistic predictions) have misled investors, causing them losses," said the third broker.

"Securities authorities should ask these companies to explain why there is such a big gap between what they have achieved and what they have forecast," he added, saying there should be rules to protect investors from losses resulting from unrealistic profit outlooks. ($1=8.3 yuan)
